question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of microsoft_docs_search, query "Azure Functions durable orchestration", to the endpoint with maxTokenBudget=2000, jsonrpc 2.0, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.what-it-answered: HTTP 200, 26155 raw bytes, 12675 content bytes (12675 characters, equal here because this content is pure ASCII), 10 results, content sha256 prefix 2533a437d96d7428.
decoded.the-vendor-claim-under-test: the vendor README, under Token Budget Control: "To manage token usage and control costs, you can append the maxTokenBudget query parameter to the MCP endpoint URL. This parameter limits the token count in search tool responses by truncating the content to meet your specified budget", marked experimental and "subject to change".
decoded.what-the-two-byte-counts-mean: two byte counts are reported because they measure different things: CONTENT bytes is the UTF-8 length of result.content[0].text, the documentation actually delivered, and RAW is the whole event-stream response. The content sha256 prefix is published so a reader can compare responses across these records without trusting a length. Only bytes were measured; the vendor's claim is about TOKENS and this record does not convert between them.
decoded.the-claim-is-measured-true: 12,675 content bytes against the unbudgeted 28,958 for the same query in the same pass (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-search-unbudgeted), so the documented parameter does cap the response for an anonymous caller, and the content sha differs from the baseline's.
decoded.but-the-result-count-does-not-change: ten results here and ten unbudgeted, and ten again at maxTokenBudget=200 (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-max-token-budget-200). The parameter truncates each chunk's content; it does not return fewer complete results. An agent budgeting its context therefore gets ten stubs rather than two whole articles and cannot choose the other trade. No vendor page read on this date says which way it truncates.
decoded.not-measured: whether the truncation is by tokens of a named tokenizer or by some proxy for them, and whether maxTokenBudget affects microsoft_code_sample_search or microsoft_docs_fetch; the vendor's wording says "search tool responses".
decoded.why-this-record-is-one-request: this pull request's records were split so that each is ONE request with one status and one surface, which is what the probe schema's own title says a probe is, after the registry's reviewer held the first head for bundling five different endpoint URLs under one observed.status and one surface. The comparison across budgets lives in the entry's profile and in the decoded fields here, each naming the sibling record it compares with.
decoded.which-reading-this-is: third reading. The five budget requests were sent once at about 12:15Z, again at 12:22:33Z when the raw byte counts were added, and again at 18:06Z as five separately captured requests. Every content and raw figure is identical across all three readings, six hours apart, so the search index behind this query did not move today.

finding: Microsoft's documented maxTokenBudget query parameter works for an anonymous caller: the same query that returns 28,958 content bytes unbudgeted returns 12,675 at maxTokenBudget=2000, measured 2026-09-30 and identical across three readings six hours apart. A vendor claim measured true. One thing the vendor does not state is visible in the same response: the RESULT COUNT is ten, exactly as it is unbudgeted and at maxTokenBudget=200, so the parameter truncates each chunk's content rather than returning fewer complete results. An agent budgeting its context gets ten stubs instead of a few whole articles and has no way to ask for the other trade. Only bytes were measured; the vendor's claim is about tokens and this record does not convert between them.

reproducibility.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp?maxTokenBudget=2000' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"microsoft_docs_search","arguments":{"query":"Azure Functions durable orchestration"}}}' | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | python3 -c 'import json,sys,hashlib;t=json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]["content"][0]["text"];print(len(t.encode()),len(json.loads(t)["results"]),hashlib.sha256(t.encode()).hexdigest()[:16])'
